correctness.rationale: For a \(\mathbb B\)-linear leakage map, the set of scalars preserving its kernel is closed under field operations; finite-dimensionality upgrades nonzero inclusion to equality, giving a subfield. Such scalars descend to linear maps on the quotient, so every computed-block leakage with coefficients in the common stabilizer factors through input-block leakage. For a nonzero one-symbol trace functional, nondegeneracy of the finite-field trace pairing forces the stabilizer to be exactly \(\mathbb B\). The product/base repair equivalence and Kronecker rank factorization then follow. An independent GF(8)/GF(2) reconstruction recovered kernel \([0,2,4,6]\) and stabilizer \([0,1]\).
